key_insight: Adaptive mesh neural operators should decide both where to compute and how to align representations across changing meshes, using gauge-aware transport to make interaction consistent and interpretable.
engineering_relevance: This can improve PDE surrogate models on nonuniform geometries by reducing discretization-induced mismatch and making adaptive computation more reliable for deployment.
method: Physics-informed adaptive allocation chooses mesh locations for computation.
Geometry-conditioned low-rank gauge transport maps source features into target node contexts before aggregation.
Operator readability is used to inspect and intervene on allocation and interaction separately.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on five PDE benchmarks, with accuracy gains plus controlled intervention and geometric-mismatch studies showing improved cross-discretization compatibility.
watch_item: Gauge transport adds modeling and implementation complexity, and its benefits may depend on preserving mesh topology and accurately conditioning on geometry.
paper_title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport
